hero.title: Provider Evaluation & RFP
hero.subtitle: Independent provider evaluations that help retirement plan committees make confident, well-documented decisions.

blocks.text: Choosing or replacing a retirement plan recordkeeper is one of the most significant fiduciary decisions a committee makes. While fees matter, they represent only one part of the evaluation. Technology, participant experience, cybersecurity, compliance support, service quality, investment flexibility, and administrative capabilities all affect the long-term success of your retirement plan.

PointOak Retirement Advisors provides independent 401(k) recordkeeper evaluation and retirement plan RFP consulting that helps committees compare providers using consistent evaluation criteria—not sales presentations. Our structured process documents every step, creating the fiduciary record your committee needs to support its decisions.

body.text: Every provider is evaluated using identical criteria, allowing your committee to compare capabilities, pricing, participant services, and technology on equal terms.
A documented evaluation process demonstrates that provider selection followed a prudent, repeatable methodology rather than subjective preference.

Modern retirement plans depend on intuitive participant websites, mobile access, education tools, payroll integration, and responsive customer service. We evaluate every aspect of the participant experience.
Even when you retain your current provider, a structured evaluation often improves pricing, service commitments, and contract terms.
Technology, cybersecurity, compliance support, payroll integration, and operational processes all affect participant outcomes. Independent evaluation helps identify risks before they become problems.

blocks.text: PointOak develops standardized evaluation criteria before reviewing any provider.

Every recordkeeper receives identical plan specifications and is scored using objective measures covering pricing, participant services, investment flexibility, compliance support, technology, cybersecurity, implementation resources, and ongoing service capabilities.

When appropriate, we manage the complete Request for Proposal (RFP) process, organize finalist presentations, score responses, and prepare committee-ready documentation that supports your final decision.
A comprehensive provider evaluation looks well beyond cost.

blocks.lead: Independent provider evaluation is especially valuable when:
items: Your provider contract is approaching renewal.
Your committee has never completed a formal RFP.
You recently completed a merger or acquisition.
Your provider's technology no longer meets participant expectations.
You cannot document why your current provider was selected.
Your committee wants objective market comparisons before renewing an agreement.
Organizations satisfied with their current provider can still benefit from independent benchmarking before extending a long-term contract.

sections.title: Annual Fee Review and Periodic Full Benchmarking

blocks.text: PointOak generally conducts a full plan and provider benchmark every three to five years, or sooner when circumstances warrant. In years when we are not conducting a full benchmark, we perform a fee benchmark and work with the provider to reprice the plan annually. The three-to-five-year interval is PointOak's practice, not a DOL or ERISA requirement.

items.q: When should a retirement plan conduct an RFP?

a.text: A competitive provider search may be appropriate when fee benchmarking, service concerns, organizational changes, or the broader market review warrant a more detailed comparison. A full benchmark does not automatically require changing providers.

items.q: What is the difference between benchmarking and an RFP?

a.text: Benchmarking compares your current provider against the marketplace. An RFP invites providers to submit competitive proposals. Benchmarking often determines whether a formal RFP is necessary.

items.q: What should be included in a recordkeeper evaluation?

a.text: A complete evaluation reviews fees, participant experience, technology, cybersecurity, compliance support, payroll integration, investment flexibility, implementation resources, service quality, and contractual terms.

items.q: How long does a typical 401(k) provider search take?

a.text: Timing depends on plan complexity, available information, provider responses, committee availability, and the scope of the review. The process can be adapted when information is already known or particular steps are not needed.

items.q: Can PointOak manage the entire RFP process?

a.text: PointOak can develop evaluation criteria, prepare RFP documents, coordinate provider communications, score responses, facilitate finalist presentations, assist with negotiations, and prepare committee documentation throughout the process.

items.q: Why use an independent consultant instead of letting providers manage the process?

a.text: An independent evaluation can help the committee compare providers using consistent information and criteria rather than relying on a single provider's presentation.
PointOak documents the findings, tradeoffs, and rationale supporting the committee's decision.
